summary: Destroys a mutex-protected singly-linked list. It waits on the mutex at this+0xB10 with the timeout at this+0xB14, then walks the list anchored at this+0xB00 (tail this+0xB04, cursor this+0xB08, fourth dword this+0xB0C); for every node it frees the node's data pointer when the byte flag at node+0x8 is non-zero and then frees the node itself. Afterward it zeros the four head fields, releases the mutex if one was held, and returns 0 otherwise. Called from NetworkCleanup_fbe0 (0057FBE0).

local_names.v2: head pointer this+0xB00 as an int array (v2[0..3] = head/tail/cursor/4th, v2[4] = mutex, v2[5] = timeout)
local_names.v5: current node pointer during list traversal
local_names.v4: list head when locked, else null

operations.description: Lock gate: only traverse when the mutex at this+0xB10 is non-null and WaitForSingleObject(handle, timeout at this+0xB14) returns 0 or 128 (owned/abandoned); otherwise the list head pointer is treated as null
WaitForSingleObject on the mutex handle this+0xB10 with the timeout this+0xB14 before touching the list
Empty-list guard: when this+0xB00 (first node pointer) is 0, the traversal loop body is skipped entirely

Walk the singly-linked list: read the current node from this+0xB00, follow the next pointer at node+0x4, free node data when the flag byte at node+0x8 is set, free the node, and continue until the next pointer is null
FreeWrapper_7bcf(*(LPVOID*)node) releases the node's data pointer when the byte at node+0x8 is non-zero
FreeWrapper_7bcf(node) frees the node allocation itself for every visited node
After traversal, zero the four head fields this+0xB00, this+0xB04, this+0xB08 and this+0xB0C, leaving the list empty
Release gate: only ReleaseMutex runs when the mutex handle at this+0xB10 is non-null
ReleaseMutex(this+0xB10) releases the mutex acquired at entry, ending the critical section
Return the mutex handle's prior state (0 when no mutex was held); called by NetworkCleanup_fbe0 (0057FBE0)
